---
title: "4. Number fields"
engine: pari-gp
format: html
---

`bnfinit` computes the class group and the units of a number field, which is
the expensive part; everything else is then a lookup. The second argument
asks for the full certified computation.

```{gp}
K = bnfinit(x^3 - 2, 1);
[K.disc, K.no, K.reg]
```

Discriminant $-108$, class number 1, and a regulator that is the logarithm of
the fundamental unit. An integral basis for $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt[3]{2}]$:

```{gp}
K.zk
```

```{gp}
K.fu
```

So $\sqrt[3]{2} - 1$ generates the units, up to sign.

## Splitting of primes

Each prime above $p$ has a residue degree $f$ and a ramification index $e$,
and $\sum ef = 3$. Listing $[f, e]$ for 2, 5 and 7 shows the three things
that can happen:

```{gp}
[[[pr.f, pr.e] | pr <- idealfactor(K, p)[, 1]~] | p <- [2, 5, 7]]
```

2 ramifies ($e = 3$), 5 splits into a degree-1 and a degree-2 prime, and 7
stays inert. That is exactly how $x^3 - 2$ factors modulo each:

```{gp}
[factormod(x^3 - 2, p)[, 1]~ | p <- [2, 5, 7]]
```

## Galois groups

$x^3-2$ is not normal, and gp names the group of its Galois closure:

```{gp}
polgalois(x^3 - 2)
```

A quintic whose group is everything, which is why it has no solution by
radicals:

```{gp}
polgalois(x^5 - x - 1)
```

## Choosing a better polynomial

Two polynomials can define the same field and look nothing alike.
`polredabs` picks the canonical small one:

```{gp}
polredabs(x^5 - 5*x^3 + 5*x - 7)
```

## Quadratic fields, quickly

`quadclassunit` skips the general machinery. The class number of
$\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-10007})$:

```{gp}
quadclassunit(-10007)[1]
```

Small imaginary quadratic fields of class number one — all nine of them, as
Heegner and Stark proved:

```{gp}
[d | d <- [-163..-1], isfundamental(d) && quadclassunit(d)[1] == 1]
```
